Covered with armor, as a ship or the face of a fortification; armor-plated.

examples.text: They came with horses and armored vehicles, carrying rifles and in tactical gear in the middle of what is the heart of immigrant Los Angeles. But there were few of their supposed targets to be found Monday — immigrants without documentation.

glosses: Equipped with armoured vehicles.

glosses: Covered with a hard steel plate; especially of vehicles, boats, and defenses.
Covered with iron, steel, or (loosely) any other tough metal; armor-plated.

examples.text: Unlike the average vehicle, cash delivery vans are ironclad and almost unstoppable.

In that flickering pallor it had the effect of a large and clumsy black insect, an insect the size of an ironclad cruiser, crawling obliquely to the first line of trenches and firing shots out of portholes in its side.

glosses: Solid or certain; not able to be disputed or questioned; irrefutable.

examples.text: The suspect had an ironclad alibi for his whereabouts on the night of the crime.

glosses: Rigorous; severe; exacting.

glosses: Stubborn; inflexible.

examples.text: All the previous articles had only elicited a growl here or there from a hide-bound Catholic or from an iron-clad Evangelical, but now his post-bag was full.

glosses: A ship, vessel, or vehicle with a covering of iron, steel, or (loosely) any other tough metal.

examples.text: He turned again to the nearest land ironclad, advancing now obliquely to him and not three hundred yards away, and then scrambled the ground over which he must retreat if he was not to be captured.

glosses: An armor-plated warship, (especially) one preceding the invention of harveyized steel.

examples.text: About a couple of miles out lay an ironclad very low in the water, almost, to my brother's perception, like a water-logged ship. This was the ram Thunder Child.
